title.narrative: Community led multi-sectoral lifesaving assistance for IDPs and newly affected people in hard-to-reach and underserved areas in Kayah and Southern Shan State in Myanmar

description.narrative:
ltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtThe fighting between de facto government troops and ethnic armed groups is still on-going in both Kayah and Southern Shan state, intensified armed conflict, especially on the Kayah/Southern Shan border, increased displacement and humanitarian needs. Since after the coup in 2021, approximately 180,000 IDPs across the region are displacing in more than 2000 IDPs sites. More than 300 civilians killed and at least 400 civilians injured since after the coup Currently, there are 3 types of IDPs in the Karenni regions which are 1) the IDPs staying with host community families, 2) IDPs in camps, and 3) Spontaneous and temporary displaced IDPs and the basis for targeting group IDP ( women- 6,135, girls-7976, Men-6,332 and Boys-7465, total -27,908) and Host communities ( women-1430, girls-3013, Men-1650, Boys-2802, total-8,895) in this proposed project . Multiple shocks have left people living in camps feeling helpless, prone to structural violence, abuse and mine risks. Vulnerable women and children are forced into behaviors which expose them to exploitation. This is on top of the fact that they are often burdened with unpaid housework, a complete lack of decision-making power and extremely scarce access to basic services. Conflict-affected children spread across camps and host communities with poor access to learning opportunities. Overall, these vulnerable groups are continuously prevented from accessing their rights. “Community-led multi-sectoral lifesaving assistance for IDPs and newly affected people in hard-to-reach and underserved areas in Kayah and Southern Shan State in Myanmar” provides emergency assistance in EiE, Food Security (FS), Protection, Shelter NFI and WASH and shelter/NFI activities to both IDPs and Host communities to meet these unmet needs in the existing locations of the MHF-RA2 funded consortium project across in 66 camps in Kayah and 28 camps in Southern Shan State at the hard-to-reach areas across Kayah. NFI activities to meet these unmet needs in the existing locations of the MHF SA2-funded consortium project across 4 townships in Kayah State and southern Shan.lt/pgtltp style="" class=""gt ltspan style="line-height: 107%"gtTogether with the 5 project local partners, AVSI would work on Education, FS, Protection, WASH and Shelter NFI cluster in the townships of Loikaw and Pekon KMSS Loikaw would work on EiE, Protection and FS in Hpruso and Demoso Alin Thit Social Development Group would work on EiE and protection, FS, WASH and NFI in Pekon MSDA would work on EiE , FS, WASH, NFI and protection in Demoso and Kayah Women Organization would work on EiE, FS and Shelter in Demoso and Pekon. KHAI will work FS, WASH and Shelter NFI in Hpruso. The project aims to provide critical and lifesaving assistance to affected and newly displaced people that will be resulted to urgently rebuild, protect and improve the food security, access to education increase the community’s awareness and capacity to address women, PwD and children’s rights, improve women’s participation and community-level decision making. For land mine victims, it provides Improved access to assistance. Lastly, WASH services will prevent the spread of disease and infections.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="line-height: 107%"gt Given this context, this grant request would prioritize women and children. All activities would mainstream C-19 prevention, women’s participation, accountability to affected populations (AAP) through ME and community feedback and complaints mechanisms. We will be guided by priorities in the First Standard Allocation (FSA) of the 2023 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), mainstream cross-cutting themes in protection, AAP, gender, disability inclusion Cash and Voucher Assistance. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
